speakers: Alan Dunne (co-host, allocator and macro commentator)
summary: Alan Dunne and Niels Kaastrup-Larsen review July 2024 markets (AI skepticism, Trump trade, sovereign debt), trend following, what allocators want from new managers, the Rho skew paper and the GIC/JPMorgan hedge fund allocation paper. Main conclusions: build hedge fund allocations in total-portfolio context, favour loss-mitigation strategies, and speed/carry choices trade smoothness against crisis response.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: investors seems to be rotating out of those sectors and into Industrials financials materials
claims.claim: In July 2024 investors rotated out of high-flying tech into industrials, financials and materials, partly linked to the Fed and the Trump trade.
claims.direction: Long industrials, financials, materials; short mega-cap tech

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: gen AI too much spend too little benefit question mark
claims.claim: A Goldman Sachs piece with skeptics (MIT's Acemoglu, Jim Covello) argues AI has few tasks that can be automated and is very costly.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the internet was a very cheap technology which uh allowed a lot of disruption
claims.claim: Unlike the internet, AI needs about a trillion dollars of capex on data centres and chips and cannot yet point to a complex task it will solve, so the disruption case is weaker.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: he thought it would increase us productivity by 0.5% over the next decade
claims.claim: Estimates of AI productivity range from 0.5% in total over a decade (MIT academic) to at least 0.5% a year, a huge range of expectations.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it could last another 12 18 months but if you hit a recession then that's when the the spend on this stuff comes under question
claims.claim: AI spending may continue for 12-18 months, but a recession would put it in question, leading tech to scale back and hit the whole boom; stay invested in AI infrastructure such as Nvidia meanwhile.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: for companies who've had substantial AI but are not spend but are not seeing any boost to revenue you know that they are being marked down after their earnings
claims.claim: Companies with large AI spend but no revenue boost are marked down after earnings (Salesforce example).
claims.direction: Short or underweight AI spenders without revenue lift

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: sometimes it can be good news elsewhere so you know the fact that we've seen good news for you know financials materials Industrials
claims.claim: A crowded AI rally can reverse not from AI earnings disappointment but from good news in other sectors triggering rotation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: losing a lot of money as long as all your peers are losing money that's actually not the biggest regret
claims.claim: Per Ben Hunt, the biggest regret is not making money when everyone else does, not losing alongside peers; fear of missing out and failing conventionally drive behaviour.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: most investors prefer to have a manager that claims that they know what uh where prices are going
claims.claim: Howard Marks says prediction is impossible, the premise of trend following, yet investors prefer managers who claim to know where prices go.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: Trump has gone from being about a 5050 likelihood of winning to uh on on the prediction markets on bfare 2 to one on about 67% likelihood
claims.claim: After the Biden debate, the assassination attempt and JD Vance's selection, Betfair odds moved from 50-50 to about 67% for Trump, driving talk of a Trump trade.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: we had maybe about two days of uh weakness in bonds which seemed the obvious uh expression of it
claims.claim: The bond-weakness leg of the Trump trade lasted only about two days and reversed; the trade is priced in parts but not in aggregate.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the obvious thing to say is deficits won't be coming down anytime soon
claims.claim: Whoever wins, tax cut extension and spending mean deficits stay high.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: he's talked about a 10% tariff on everything and 60% on on China
claims.claim: Tariffs of 10% on everything and 60% on China, on top of continued bipartisan China trade policy over Chinese overcapacity, make tariffs a major issue.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: his whole philosophy is around aiming for trade balance on a bilateral basis with all of the major trading partners
claims.claim: Lighthizer's bilateral trade-balance aim implies currency alignment, so dollar policy against yen and yuan could be hugely disruptive.
claims.direction: Weaker dollar vs yen and yuan

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you might want a weak dollar but can you achieve it if you're going to be cutting taxes and stimulating the economy
claims.claim: A weak dollar goal conflicts with tax cuts and stimulus, which push the dollar up.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you reverse that you've got a reduced labor Supply so that pushes up wages so that's a St inflationary impulse
claims.claim: Immigration drove the US growth surprise, so reversing it reduces labor supply, raises wages and is stagflationary (Posen).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: where you say to Japanese want you to participate in selling dollar Yen and drive it down you know they may want to sell treasuries
claims.claim: A Plaza-accord-like push for a weaker dollar needs Japan to sell dollars, but Japan may sell Treasuries to do so, which hurts US bonds and explains Yellen's reluctance.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: gold obviously starting to rise which could be reflecting that weak dollar story
claims.claim: Gold's rise might reflect the weak-dollar and Trump policy story, though other currencies have not moved much.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: when everybody sees it then everybody knows that everybody knows
claims.claim: Unsustainable debt only gets priced when a public event makes everyone know that everyone knows (emperor's new clothes), so the safe-asset status of sovereign debt could change abruptly.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: we're not seeing any change in inflation uh expectations or term Premia which you would expect
claims.claim: Despite Trump talk, inflation expectations and term premia show no change, so an event is needed to focus the market on deficits.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: higher yields makes the debt less sustainable in itself so you know Rising yields are reinforcing
claims.claim: Rising yields make debt less sustainable, which is reflexive and reinforcing, so a safe place now does not mean it will last.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if there was going to be a fiscal crisis that would probably be more politically driven
claims.claim: Posen: a fiscal crisis would probably be politically driven (debt ceiling disputes, a UK-style budget announcement) rather than market-driven.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: maybe it's the the steepener trade that a lot of people have been talking about it for a long time and that will gain traction
claims.claim: A curve steepener trade could gain traction once deficits enter market psychology.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my Trend barometer is not you know it's not firing on all cylinders it's still below neutral but it is increasing from the lows of at the end of June
claims.claim: In mid-July 2024 the Trend Barometer was below neutral but rising from late-June lows; BTOP50 about +1.5% for the month (+8.68% YTD), SG CTA about +8%, SG Trend +10.6%, versus S&P +17.8% YTD.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the downtrend in grains which uh has been quite uh beneficial for Trend following managers
claims.claim: Grains downtrend, gold's new highs, equity strength and coffee helped trend followers, while the yen's reversal hurt.
claims.direction: Short grains, long gold and equities

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: some of the markets um that were looked to be on the verge of major moves out have reversed I thinking copper
claims.claim: Markets such as copper reversed after looking set for major breakouts, giving a choppy two-to-three-month period for trend.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: some of this choppiness has actually benefited some of the replicators who trade very few markets
claims.claim: Replicators trading few markets avoided the choppiness and beat the indices they replicate in recent months.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: what's different about any new offering either from a strategy perspective or a cost perspective
claims.claim: A new trend fund must differ from the many 60-100 market trend managers in strategy (speed, sectors, concentration) or cost to attract allocators.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: small managers have some advant ages in terms of being able to be more Nimble to to be able to trade the smaller markets in in bigger risk allocations
claims.claim: Small managers can allocate more risk to smaller markets and trade faster, but if too small they cannot trade enough contracts, so there is a sweet spot in AUM.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: some of the new players coming into the industry trying to do something different are actually maybe going a little bit backwards to the to the classical style of trend following allowing it to be more volatile
claims.claim: Some new trend managers differentiate by going back to classic, more volatile trend following and trading markets large funds cannot.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: low Val 8 to 10% Vol is more of an Institutional product
claims.claim: Family offices and ultra-high-net-worth investors want higher-octane strategies, while 8-10% vol is an institutional product, so small managers pitch higher vol.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they have simply increased their performance fee from 20% to 30%
claims.claim: CFM raised its performance fee from 20% to 30%, going against the race to zero fees set by replicators and ETFs.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: plenty of allocators like that consistency of return as well and we've seen that with the uh with the huge asset flows into the multi strats
claims.claim: There is pricing power in consistent returns, shown by the rise of multi-strats and CFM's multi-strat flagship (6-8 vol, 8-10% target return).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: as soon as performance becomes more challenging then fees become becomes a conversation
claims.claim: In CTAs, fee levels are accepted while performance is consistent, but a drawdown quickly turns fees into the issue.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: accusing the the industry of kind of a lot of trend followers of of moving away from Pure Trend into things like carry
claims.claim: Asness argued that diversified trend followers adding carry to smooth returns lose risk mitigation; the Rho paper tests this.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: commodity carry uh can be very much a a Divergent U strategy from that perspective and has performed very well in in in times of of stress
claims.claim: Commodity carry reflects supply and demand imbalances rather than a risk premium, acts as a divergent strategy and did well in stress, unlike currency carry.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: picking up the pennies in front of the steamroller and one day you're going to get rolled over and have a big loss
claims.claim: Currency carry is negatively skewed, a convergence strategy with an eventual big loss.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: replicating the Delta on a straddle which is you you you increase your long exposure as the market goes up and decreases and go short as Mark Goan which is very much like Trend following
claims.claim: Convexity comes from straddles or from delta-replicating them, which is fast trend following; the paper compares fast, medium and slow trend on skewness and return.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: positive skewness is is a positive uh feature in terms of reactivity and risk mitigation
claims.claim: Negatively skewed strategies (equity-like) gain often with a left tail, whereas positive skew gives outsized gains in equity sell-offs, so it matters for risk mitigation.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you move out to things like slow Trend following and it's actually negatively it's a negatively skewed strategy when you're measured in terms of days
claims.claim: Fast trend and straddles are positively skewed, slow trend is negatively skewed in daily returns, flat in monthly and positive in quarterly.
claims.indicator: trend skewness by speed and horizon

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you trade slower you can also dampen your your risk mitigation and generate more consistent returns
claims.claim: Trend speed is another lever beside adding non-trend: slower trend smooths returns but reduces reactivity.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you combine Trend with commodity carry and add to equities you can get a better outcome than just adding Trend
claims.claim: Adding trend plus commodity carry to equities beats trend alone in skewness and return.
claims.indicator: trend plus commodity carry overlay on equities

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: long-term ass ators think in terms of quarterly hot time Horizons
claims.claim: Long-term allocators think in quarterly horizons, so negative daily skew in slow trend may not matter; it depends on the investor.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the sharpest and and sort of um meaningful Corrections that that we as Trend followers will experience uh in our performance actually also comes at a time where we making the most money
claims.claim: Man AHL research after the SVB event: the sharpest trend drawdown weeks tend to occur in periods of strong trends and high volatility when trend is making most money.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you shouldn't worry about five- day returns you should worried about 5 years 10 years 20 year returns
claims.claim: Long-horizon investors should judge trend following on 5-20 year returns, not on 5-day protection.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: all of these uh make asset allocation via long only return streams across public and private markets more challenging
claims.claim: GIC and JPMorgan paper: regime shift (geopolitics, fragmentation, higher inflation, rates and vol) makes long-only allocation harder, so investors seek alpha over beta and hedge funds.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: over half of the head hedge funds had a correlation of less than 0.5 to equities
claims.claim: Of about 1,000 hedge funds over 13 years, over half had equity correlation below 0.5; managed futures, commodity and macro were least correlated, all managed futures strategies under 0.5.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they had 30 to 40% of multi strats and RV funds had a correlation of 0.5 or higher so again these types of strategies um very popular but not necessarily strong diversifiers
claims.claim: 30-40% of multi-strat and relative-value funds had equity correlation of 0.5 or higher, so these popular strategies are not necessarily strong diversifiers.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: manage features uh doing well in that scenario
claims.claim: In equity declines managed futures preserved capital and showed good alpha, whereas relative value, credit and event driven did not.
claims.indicator: hedge fund returns in equity drawdowns

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: then they used a clustering technique to group the managers into four groups based on the manager characteristics
claims.claim: Clustering on correlation, drawdown resilience and alpha gave four groups: loss mitigation, equity diversifier, equity complement and equity substitute; managed futures fell into the first two.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they all mapped to all of the these four categories so highlighting the the the the kind of um dispersion that you see across managers
claims.claim: Every strategy label contains funds in every cluster, so the label does not tell the role and manager-level dispersion matters.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you bring it into a 6040 portfolio and reoptimize then you go 100% to loss mitigation and not only that you can actually lever up your equities a bit more
claims.claim: A standalone hedge fund portfolio was about 59% loss mitigation, 19% equity diversifier and 22% equity complement, but inside a 60/40 re-optimization it goes 100% loss mitigation and allows more equity leverage.
claims.direction: Loss-mitigation hedge funds with more equities

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you don't need to get Equity beta from hedge funds you can get Equity beta from equities and get diversification uh from hedge fund
claims.claim: Get equity beta from equities and use hedge funds for diversification.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: ctas had been long bonds for for a long time but obviously by virtue of the of of understanding the strategy you know that they can turn short
claims.claim: Manager selection requires understanding the strategy, because a past pattern (CTAs long bonds) reflects the market and can reverse or chop.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they say 15 to 20 is is the optimal that they came up but diversification benefits decline after that
claims.claim: The optimal number of hedge fund managers is 15-20; more is justified for tactical reasons.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: there's an incentive fee if you terminate a manager in a drone and you're giving up basically the the Free Ride you have back up to the the high Watermark
claims.claim: Terminating a manager in drawdown gives up the free ride back to the high-watermark, so the replacement must be better by more than the forgone incentive fee.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: there can be a case for having emerging managers um you know particularly if other manager are closed or just from the perspective of building capacity
claims.claim: Emerging managers can be added for capacity and because they are more niche, smaller and nimble.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: pure loss mitigation type strategies can be a tough hold you know there's draw Downs
claims.claim: Pure loss mitigation strategies are hard to hold when equity beta does well, so allocators may sweeten with more consistent strategies even if the numbers do not justify it.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it also has that marking time Market timing element it has this risk on element to it at times as well
claims.claim: Trend following is not only loss mitigation; it also has a market-timing risk-on element at times.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it that forgets the fact that you're build building this portfolio in the context of the overall portfolio
claims.claim: Building a hedge fund portfolio on diversification alone (convergent plus divergent) forgets that it should be built in the context of the overall portfolio.
